notes.summary:
Software and operating systems gives 2 to 4 questions in Tier 2. Expect questions on system vs application software, open-source and free software, what an operating system does and its types, OS terms like spooling and virtual memory, Windows keyboard shortcuts, utility programs, and compilers, interpreters and assemblers.

Almost all are fact questions. The tables below cover what has been asked.

concepts.title: What software is
concepts.body:
Software is a set of programs (instructions) that tells the hardware what to do. There are two big groups:

System softwareApplication software
Runs and manages the computer itselfDoes a job for the user
Operating system, device drivers, utility programs, language translators, firmware (BIOS)MS Word, Excel, web browsers, Tally, games, media players
Starts when the computer starts; works in the backgroundRuns only when the user opens it
  • General-purpose application software does common jobs (word processor, spreadsheet). Specific-purpose or tailor-made software is built for one task (railway reservation, payroll).
  • A device driver lets the operating system talk to one piece of hardware, such as a printer.
  • Middleware connects applications to each other or to the OS. An application server gives developers a set of components through an API defined by the platform.

concepts.title: Operating system: jobs and parts
concepts.body:
The operating system (OS) is the main system software. It sits between the user and the hardware and manages all resources.

  • Process management: starts, stops and schedules programs on the CPU.
  • Memory management: gives RAM to programs and takes it back.
  • File management: creates, names, stores and protects files and folders.
  • Device management: controls hardware through drivers.
  • Security: passwords, user accounts, permissions.
  • User interface: CLI (command line, typed commands, like MS-DOS) or GUI (graphical, with icons and windows, like Windows).
  • The kernel is the core of the OS; it stays in memory and talks directly to the hardware.
  • The shell is the layer that takes the user's commands and passes them to the kernel.
  • Desktop and laptop operating systems need more advanced memory management than embedded systems because they run many different programs at the same time; an embedded system runs one fixed job.

concepts.title: Types of operating systems
concepts.body:
TypeIdea
BatchSimilar jobs are grouped and run one after another with no user interaction
MultiprogrammingSeveral programs kept in memory so the CPU is never idle
Time-sharing (multitasking)CPU time is split into small slices so many users or tasks seem to run together
MultiprocessingTwo or more CPUs work together
Real-time (RTOS)Must respond within a fixed time: missiles, air-traffic control, medical machines
DistributedMany connected computers act as one system
NetworkRuns on a server and manages shared resources over a network
Embedded and mobileBuilt into devices (washing machines) or phones (Android, iOS)
OSMade by / note
MS-DOSMicrosoft; single-user, command line
WindowsMicrosoft; GUI
UnixBell Labs (1969), Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie; multi-user
LinuxLinus Torvalds (1991); open source. Distributions: Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian
macOS and iOSApple
AndroidGoogle; built on the Linux kernel
Chrome OSGoogle

concepts.title: Operating system terms
concepts.body:
• Booting: loading the OS into RAM when the computer starts. The BIOS in ROM checks the hardware (POST) and then starts the bootstrap loader.
  • Spooling (Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line): jobs for a slow device such as a printer are put in a queue on disk, so the CPU can go on with other work.
  • Buffering: holding data in a temporary memory area while it moves between devices.
  • Virtual memory: part of the hard disk used as an extension of RAM. Data moves in fixed blocks called pages (paging).
  • Thrashing: the system spends more time swapping pages than doing real work.
  • Deadlock: two or more processes wait for each other forever, so none can go on.
  • Process: a program while it is running. A thread is a smaller unit of a process.
  • Plug and play: the OS detects a new device and sets it up by itself.
  • Automatic updates: the OS downloads and installs security patches without the user doing anything.

concepts.title: Files and folders
concepts.body:
• A file is a named collection of data. A folder (directory) holds files and other folders (subfolders).
  • Folders form a tree. The top folder of a drive is the root directory, for example C:\.
  • A path gives the location: C:\Users\Ravi\notes.txt.
  • The extension after the dot tells the file type.
  • Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin and can be restored. Shift + Delete skips the Recycle Bin.
ExtensionFile type

concepts.title: Utility programs
concepts.body:
Utilities are small system programs that keep the computer healthy.

UtilityWhat it does
AntivirusFinds and removes malware (Quick Heal, Norton, McAfee, Windows Defender)
Disk CleanupDeletes temporary and unneeded files to free space
Disk DefragmenterPuts the scattered pieces of files back together so the disk reads faster
BackupCopies data so it can be restored after loss
File compressionMakes files smaller (WinZip, WinRAR, 7-Zip)
Control PanelShows a list of tools to configure the system and to add or remove hardware and software
Task ManagerShows running programs, CPU and memory use; can end a program that is not responding
Device ManagerLists hardware and their drivers
System RestoreTakes the system settings back to an earlier point

concepts.title: Programming languages
concepts.body:
LevelWhat it isExample
Machine language (1st generation)Only 0s and 1s; the CPU understands it directly; fastest; machine dependent10110000 01100001
Assembly language (2nd)Short words called mnemonicsADD, MOV, SUB
High-level language (3rd)English-like, machine independent; needs a compiler or interpreterC, C++, Java, Python, FORTRAN, COBOL
4th generationSays what to do, not how; close to EnglishSQL
5th generationUsed for AI and logicProlog
  • FORTRAN (formula translation): science and maths. COBOL: business. BASIC: beginners.
  • C: Dennis Ritchie (1972). C++: Bjarne Stroustrup. Java: James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (1995). Python: Guido van Rossum (1991).
  • HTML is a markup language, not a programming language.
  • Source code is what the programmer writes; object code is the translated machine code. An error in a program is a bug; removing it is debugging.

concepts.title: Language translators
concepts.body:
TranslatorConvertsHow
AssemblerAssembly language to machine codeInstruction by instruction
CompilerHigh-level language to machine codeWhole program in one go; lists all errors at the end; the program then runs fast (C, C++)
InterpreterHigh-level language to machine codeOne line at a time; stops at the first error; slower to run (Python, BASIC)
  • A linker joins object files and library code into one executable program.
  • A loader puts the executable program into memory so it can run.
  • Java is first compiled to bytecode, which the Java Virtual Machine then runs.

varieties.name: Types of software and licences
varieties.how: Ask: does it run the computer (system) or do a job for the user (application)? For licences ask: is the code open, free, or free only for a trial?

example.q: Which of the following is not a LibreOffice program: Writer, Calc, Impress, Excel?
steps: LibreOffice has Writer, Calc, Impress, Draw, Base and Math.
Excel is part of Microsoft Office.

varieties.name: Operating systems: types, functions and terms
varieties.how: Link each term to its one-line meaning: spooling is a print queue, virtual memory is disk used as RAM, real-time means a fixed response time.

example.q: Which type of operating system is used in air-traffic control, where every response must come within a fixed time?
steps: Batch systems run jobs with no time promise.
Time-sharing systems share the CPU but do not guarantee a deadline.
A real-time OS guarantees a response within a fixed time.

varieties.name: Windows shortcuts and file management
varieties.how: Windows key combos open system tools (E Explorer, D desktop, L lock, R Run, I Settings). Alt + Enter is Properties; F2 is rename.

example.q: Which keyboard shortcut opens File Explorer in Windows?
steps: Windows key + D shows the desktop.
Windows key + E opens File Explorer (E for Explorer).

varieties.name: Utility programs and system tools
varieties.how: Match the tool to its job: defragmenter joins file pieces, cleanup frees space, compression shrinks files, Control Panel changes settings.

example.q: Which utility rearranges the scattered parts of files on a hard disk so it can read them faster?
steps: Disk Cleanup deletes files; it does not rearrange them.
Disk Defragmenter puts the pieces of each file next to each other.

varieties.name: Programming languages and translators
varieties.how: Compiler = whole program at once; interpreter = line by line; assembler = assembly to machine code. Linker joins, loader loads.

example.q: Which program translates and runs a high-level program one line at a time?
steps: A compiler translates the whole program in one go.
An assembler works on assembly language, not high-level code.
An interpreter works line by line.

tips: The operating system is system software; MS Word, Excel and browsers are application software.
Windows key + E opens File Explorer; Alt + Enter opens Properties; Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager.
Spooling = Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line; think of a print queue.
Linux, LibreOffice, Firefox, VLC and Android are open source; Windows and MS Office are proprietary.
Compiler: whole program at once, fast to run. Interpreter: line by line, stops at the first error.
Android is built on the Linux kernel; Unix came from Bell Labs.
traps: Freeware is free to use but not open source; do not mix them up.
An assembler translates assembly language, not a high-level language.
Shift + Delete deletes permanently; plain Delete sends the file to the Recycle Bin.
Virtual memory uses the hard disk, not the cache or ROM.
HTML is a markup language, not a programming language.

questions.q: Which of the following is system software?
questions.solution: The operating system manages the hardware and runs the computer, so it is system software. The others do user tasks and are application software.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an operating system?
questions.solution: MS Excel is a spreadsheet application. Linux, Windows 11 and Android are operating systems.

questions.q: A translator that converts the whole high-level program into machine code in one go is called a(n):
questions.solution: A compiler translates the entire program at once. An interpreter goes line by line; an assembler converts assembly language.

questions.q: The small program that starts the computer and checks the hardware, stored in ROM, is the:
questions.solution: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is firmware in ROM. It runs the POST check and then loads the operating system into RAM.
An assembler translates assembly language mnemonics (like ADD, MOV) into machine code (binary).

questions.q: In operating systems, SPOOL stands for:
questions.solution: SPOOL = Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line. Jobs such as print jobs are stored on disk in a queue and sent to the slow device one by one.

questions.q: Which of the following is open-source software?
questions.solution: LibreOffice's source code is freely available and can be changed. MS Office, Photoshop and Windows are proprietary.

questions.q: Virtual memory lets a computer use part of the ___ as an extension of RAM.
questions.solution: Virtual memory uses space on secondary storage (hard disk / SSD), called the page file or swap space, as if it were extra RAM.

flashcards.back: System software runs the computer (OS, drivers, utilities); application software does user tasks (Word, Excel, Tally).
Compiler: whole program at once. Interpreter: line by line.
Loading the operating system into RAM. Cold boot = from off; warm boot = restart.
Part of the hard disk used as an extension of RAM
The core of the operating system that controls hardware, memory and processes
Software free for a trial period; then you must pay
